memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, together with Moses' sons and wife, came to him
in the wilderness, where he was camped near the mountain of God. Jethro had sent
word to him, 'I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and
her two sons.'" - Ex 18:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jethro comes, and he brings Moses' family back to him.

There is a lovely thoughtfulness in the detail that he sent word ahead. He did
not simply arrive. He let Moses know he was coming and who was with him.

That is a small kindness worth learning from. Jethro considered how his arrival
would land. In a season when Moses was carrying an enormous weight, an
unannounced arrival, even a welcome one, would have been one more thing to
absorb.

Notice where the reunion happens: "in the wilderness, where he was camped near
the mountain of God." Moses is in a hard, demanding place. And that is where his
family comes to him.

Sometimes God brings people to us in the wilderness rather than removing us from
it. The help arrives inside the difficulty, not instead of it.

Notice also that Moses is reunited with his wife and sons here. Whatever strain
had led to their separation, this is a restoration. Leadership had cost Moses
time with his family, as it often does. God brings them back.

If ministry or work has quietly crowded out the people closest to you, this
chapter is worth sitting with.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has your work or service crowded out those closest to you?
2. Who might need you to think ahead about how your arrival will land?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for bringing people to me in hard places. Help me not to
neglect those closest to me while I serve others. Amen.
